articles.text:
Sensible Biotechnologies Raises $47 Million To Advance Naturally Modified mRNA Platform
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 6, 2026
Sensible Biotechnologies Raises $47 Million To Advance Naturally Modified mRNA Platform
Sensible Biotechnologies has secured $47 million in financing to advance and scale its platform for naturally modified mRNA medicines. The financing includes a Series A led by Oxford Science Enterprises and up to $20 million of non-dilutive funding from the Government of Slovakia and the European Union.
New investors OTB Ventures and In-Q-Tel participated in the Series A alongside existing investors Recode Ventures, Isomer Capital, Y Combinator, Backed VC, Kaya VC, Civilization Ventures and BlueYard Capital.
Individual investors included the family office of BioNTech co-founder Christoph Huber and former Eli Lilly Chief Medical Officer Tim Garnett.
Sensible plans to use the capital to expand its VECTOR platform, AI-enabled mRNA design and automated high-throughput screening capabilities and establish clinical-grade manufacturing.
The company’s approach differs from conventional synthetic mRNA manufacturing by using engineered living cells to manufacture naturally modified mRNA.
VECTOR combines computational and AI-enabled sequence optimization, high-throughput screening and proprietary engineered eukaryotic cells.
Sensible’s PromPT technology captures and protects mRNA inside cells before purification.
The company said the approach is designed to reduce immunogenicity and provide high protein expression while avoiding double-stranded RNA contamination that can cause unwanted immune activation.
External evaluations showed no detectable double-stranded RNA contamination, reduced cytokine activation and higher protein expression compared with synthetic mRNA in human immune-cell assays, according to Sensible.
Dr. Vishal Gulati of Recode Ventures and Joel Schoppig of Oxford Science Enterprises will join Sensible’s Board as part of the financing.
KEY QUOTES:
“mRNA transformed vaccines, but we believe its greatest potential lies in therapeutics. The field still relies largely on synthetic manufacturing technology developed more than 40 years ago. We are taking a fundamentally different approach, using living cells to produce naturally modified mRNA while reducing the cost and supply-chain constraints of conventional production. With this financing, we can scale our platform and expand mRNA into therapeutic applications requiring high or repeated dosing that have historically been limited by cost.”
Miroslav Gasparek, Chief Executive Officer and Co-Founder of Sensible Biotechnologies
“The promise of computational drug design depends on connecting it to biology and the practical work of making a medicine. How mRNA is made can shape how it behaves, so manufacturing matters from the very start of developing a treatment. Sensible brings design and cell-based production together, giving the team an opportunity to improve both the performance of mRNA and the economics of making it. We led this round because we believe in the team’s ability to build a company that helps pharmaceutical partners develop a broader range of mRNA medicines. With this investment, Sensible can advance toward clinical-grade production and expand the pharmaceutical partnerships that will drive its commercial growth.”
Joel Schoppig, Partner at Oxford Science Enterprises and Board Member at Sensible

articles.text:
WILDE Raises $40 Million From S2G Investments To Expand Protein Snack Production And Product Innovation
By Amit Chowdhry
Oct 22, 2026
WILDE Raises $40 Million From S2G Investments To Expand Protein Snack Production And Product Innovation
WILDE, a Lexington, Kentucky-based snack company specializing in protein-rich chips and crackers, has secured a $40 million investment from S2G Investments. The financing will support manufacturing expansion, new product development, and marketing initiatives as the company builds on more than $100 million in sales and distribution across over 35,000 retail locations nationwide.
Founded in 2015 by Jason Wright, WILDE has developed a portfolio of salty snacks made primarily from natural chicken breast, egg whites, and bone broth. Its products are designed to provide the taste and texture associated with traditional snack foods while delivering higher protein content.
The company’s Protein Chips and Protein Crackers offer more than 10 grams of protein per serving, positioning the brand within the growing market for snacks that combine convenience, flavor, and nutritional benefits.
WILDE recently opened a 130,000-square-foot manufacturing facility designed to substantially expand its production capabilities. According to the company, the facility is the only USDA-regulated salty snack manufacturing plant in the world.
The new operation increases WILDE’s production capacity sixfold, providing additional infrastructure to serve its expanding retail distribution network and introduce new products.
The $40 million investment will help the company scale manufacturing operations while broadening its product portfolio beyond its original Protein Chips.
Following the recent introduction of Protein Crackers, WILDE is developing additional snack formats intended to reach new consumers and address a wider variety of eating occasions.
The financing will also support improvements to the company’s visual identity, product packaging, and marketing capabilities as it seeks to establish greater recognition in the broader packaged food industry.
S2G Investments sees an opportunity to expand WILDE’s position as consumers increasingly seek convenient foods that deliver additional nutritional value, particularly protein.
The investment firm focuses on businesses operating across food and agriculture, energy, and oceans. Its investment capabilities include growth equity, structured finance, and other forms of capital designed to help companies expand their operations.
For WILDE, the investment provides resources to support the next phase of growth following the development of a national retail footprint and substantial investments in manufacturing infrastructure.
The company plans to use its expanded production capacity and new product development initiatives to reach additional consumers while maintaining its focus on protein-forward snacks.
KEY QUOTES:
“Building WILDE has never been easy. We started this company to prove that protein snacks don’t have to taste like punishment, and we’ve spent years betting on an idea that didn’t fit neatly into the snack aisle. We stuck with it, built something people crave, and this investment proves that hard work and conviction pay off. Now we have the firepower to go bigger, move faster, and shake up a whole lot more of the snack aisle.”
Jason Wright, Founder And CEO Of WILDE
